analysis:
The only change in this PR is one added documentation row in docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 417): `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP`. The row describes a load-time shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots. Values `0`/`false`/`no`/`off` disable it, `always` skips the probe, and unset runs a probe-gated warmup. The probe is a 128-token shader-cache check run twice, and shape cells run only on a cold cache, capped at 20 seconds per engine. The row says the variable is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. Both supplied units are base text; the one-line head addition appears only in the patch excerpt, which is truncated, so there is no head-side line to cite.

This is a documentation-only change with no code, auth, attestation, crypto or data-handling changes. It does not affect the A-001 prompt confidentiality assumptions, the prefix-cache threat T-041 or the attestation and App Attest authorization boundaries (TB-011, T-052 to T-058). The warmup is described as training no rate or counter, so it does not obviously alter deadline-admission or calibration state.

Open questions for integration, which I cannot verify from this evidence. First, whether the warmup uses synthetic tokens only and never real consumer prompt content, which would matter for T-028 residual GPU data. Second, whether the LaunchAgent passthrough allowlist in LaunchAgent.swift actually includes this key as the doc claims. Third, whether any warmup-populated cache could interact with the prefix cache or timing oracle (SEC-035). The reviewed documentation does not suggest any of these. I did not review the code, so no regression is claimed or excluded beyond the documentation text.
